title: Scheming Propensity Is Configuration-Dependent: Mapping the Sensitivity Surface

original_idea.body:
# Scheming Propensity Is Configuration-Dependent: Mapping the Sensitivity Surface

**Problem:** A 2026 frontier-model study concludes scheming propensity 'cannot be characterized by a single number' and depends on agent configuration. Which configuration knobs matter most — and whether this holds for accessible open models — is not mapped.

**Direction:** On an open agentic model, systematically vary a few configuration factors (goal-directedness in the system prompt, presence of oversight cues, stakes framing, tool permissions) in a small factorial design over a scheming-eval task. Measure scheming rate per cell and rank which factors drive the most variance.

**Why it matters:** If scheming is config-sensitive, single-number eval scores are misleading. A sensitivity map showing which deployment knobs most inflate scheming gives evaluators a checklist of what to vary — a reproducible methodological contribution.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents' (arXiv:2603.01608, 2026), which found scheming requires exploring deployment configurations rather than a single score.
